sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, Adil Shahis, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct full article read; dynasty, wars and commerce. Founding date varies 1489/1490 across reference works; public prose says around 1490. Do not equate the 1565 defeat with complete extinction of Vijayanagara.

sources.title: Muhammad Baqir, Bijapur, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct article read; Persian literary culture and 1686 annexation. Geographical introductory wording is not used.

sources.title: Namrata B. Kanchan, Political notes of nauras, Modern Asian Studies (2026)
sources.note: Direct full text. Figure 1 and notes 3-4 distinguish Ismail’s reading of the stylized coin from literal letter placement; translation protector of the weak is Kanchan’s. Chand Bibi death date and disputed exact songbook date omitted.

sources.title: Radhika Seshan, Kiran Jadhav and Nalini Avinash Waghmare, Urban Patterns in Medieval Deccan, IGNOU Unit 10
sources.note: Official PDF downloaded to urban-history.pdf and extracted with pypdf. Printed pages 169 and 173-176, PDF pages 15 and 19-22. Asad Beg’s bazaar description remains explicitly attributed; no universal sanitation or household plumbing inference.

sources.title: Christopher D. Bahl, Histories of Circulation: Sharing Arabic Manuscripts across the Western Indian Ocean (SOAS thesis, 2018)
sources.note: Direct PDF open failed. Indexed original repository PDF was read at printed p121, including note 539. Reproducible query: site.eprints.soas.ac.uk/30302/1/4592_Bahl.pdf "Modi". Only the directly indexed paragraph and manuscript marginalia claim are used.

sources.title: K. W. Wiggins, A Larin Hoard from the North Konkan, ONS Newsletter 54 (1978)
sources.note: Direct PDF read, pages 2-3. Reproduces 1848-1849 correspondence; author corrects its date conversions and questions exchange rate. Use hoard count, discovery context and physical form only, not erroneous historical dates or exchange rate.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Ibrahim Rouza
sources.note: Direct monument page read. Family tomb, mosque, tank and carved calligraphic windows. No unsupported structural explanation or exact ruler death year inferred from monument completion.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Gol Gumbaz
sources.note: Direct monument page read. Brick dome, eight intersecting arches, whispering gallery and burials. Omit page’s inconsistent Muhammad II label, disputed completion date and world-size superlatives.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The House of Bijapur, about 1680
sources.note: Direct collection record read. Kamal Muhammad and Chand Muhammad; imagined dynastic assembly for Sikandar. Do not repeat inconsistent count of rulers; later inscription misidentifies Shah Ismail as Abbas.

proposedOverrides.name: Bijapur (Adil Shahi Sultanate)
proposedOverrides.summary: The Adil Shahi sultanate linked Deccan power, coastal commerce and a celebrated artistic court.

batchIdentityNotes.historicalIdentity: Adil Shahi Sultanate of Bijapur, around 1490-1686
batchIdentityNotes.interpretation: The five imported snapshots retain almost the same outline. This is an approximate western Deccan footprint, not a reconstruction of every historical frontier or later southern expansion. Indexed date coverage extends beyond the Mughal conquest. Public overview and ending qualify this.
